narrative.overview: The window is a marbler's tray of size. Each scene lays pigment on the water, and the trained network's predicted velocity carries it live beside the pulled print of the reference. A daylight, matte world of grey-green size, wet tray, deckled paper and ink; the dark ParaView-style viewer is the anti-reference. Numbers show their source: measured in solid stamped type, live-derived in hairline. Passing and failing scenes get the same care, and every failure shows its evidence.
keyCharacteristics: One historic marbling pigment per scene, everywhere that scene appears
OKLab data colour maps interpolated from the pigments
Procedural materials made at run time; no raster files ship
Every choice on screen, the active one struck forward

rules.name: The Pigment Is the Scene Rule
rules.body: A scene's pigment never appears on another scene's controls; dropped pigment is the only exception.

rules.name: The Data Colour Rule
rules.body: Field views use the OKLab sequential, diverging and error maps only; decorative pigment never encodes a value.

rules.name: The 13 Pixel Floor
rules.body: No text in the window is smaller than 13 px.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Tabular lining figures for every number; one scientific notation (4.2e-5); a live percentage takes the measured headline's precision.

rules.name: The No Stacked Offsets Rule
rules.body: A shadow is one blurred mask, never stacked zero-blur offsets.

dos: Do put a scene's labels on the tray's lip
Do show every measured number with its source, every live number in hairline
Do veil the pigment to 20% over a data view
Do give failing scenes their specific evidence on screen
Do make materials procedurally, cached per pixel size
donts: Don't use a dark viewport, a scene tree or a property panel
Don't set text in a pigment; ochre is a rule and marker colour
Don't draw a missing value as zero
Don't claim the networks are faster or cheaper than a CFD solver
